items.title: When Should AI Agents Ask? Clarification Requests Under Limited Human Attention
items.abstract: AI agents increasingly carry out delegated tasks in parallel, with one person overseeing several of them at once. In practice, an agent often lacks information its task requires, such as an unstated preference, constraint, or specification. It can ask the human to clarify, or it can search for the information itself, for example in past records, which takes time and effort and may fail. In this paper, we study how to coordinate these decisions across several agents that share one human with limited attention. We build a stylized model in which each agent can search, ask, or continue the parts of its task that do not depend on the missing information, and we formulate the problem as a dynamic program. We first show that whether an agent should ask depends on more than its own uncertainty: an agent with other work to do can be better off asking earlier, and which question the human should answer first depends on all waiting questions, so no ranking computed agent by agent is optimal. We then propose the Pairwise Coordination Policy (PCP), which uses exact one- and two-task problems to estimate how pairs of tasks delay each other when they share the human. Theoretically, PCP is exactly optimal when at most two requirements remain unresolved and costs at most twice the optimum when every unresolved requirement must be resolved by the human. We evaluate PCP on 864 synthetic cases and in a case study with LLM agents. On the synthetic benchmark, PCP's mean gap to optimal cost is 0.07%, and it reduces cost by an average of 18-31% relative to three standard rules for when to ask. In the LLM case study, agents completed every task correctly, and PCP achieved the lowest mean cost in all tested settings.

items.title: When Steering Shifts Discourse: Identifying and Intervening on Discourse-Level Changes due to Activation Steering in LLMs
items.abstract: Activation steering is an inference-time technique used to control or modify the behavior, tone, or safety properties of a large language model (LLM) without retraining the model's weights or editing its input prompt, but simply by adding a vector to its residual-stream activations. However, activation steering also changes the generated text in unintended ways, unrelated to intended behavior change, that are not well understood. Prior work has measured these changes only through coarse signals such as perplexity. In this work, we show that steering systematically produces significant changes in discourse dimensions of the generated text, such as its formality, use of evidence, and ambiguity. We present a way of countering this by adding a second, complementary vector that targets the affected discourse dimension. This intervention restores about 78% of the unintended discourse changes while preserving the intended steering behavior in about 93% of the generations.

items.title: When the Past Shapes Action: Understanding Embodied Memory
items.abstract: Recent advances in generative foundation models have expanded the capabilities of embodied AI, enabling increasingly general navigation, manipulation, and long-horizon task execution. However, effective interaction with dynamic environments requires more than only strong perception and reasoning: agents must act with partial knowledge and retain, retrieve, and update information from past observations, actions, and experiences. This survey examines embodied memory as a mechanism for preserving decision-relevant information beyond the current observation. We organize existing approaches along two complementary dimensions: six fundamental memory requirements, spanning world-state persistence, task progress, belief maintenance, and experiential learning; and eight architectural categories, including recurrent states, fast weights, visual and symbolic representations, spatial memory, and experience-based systems. We analyze their capabilities and limitations, and examine how existing benchmarks evaluate memory-dependent behavior, distinguishing genuine use of historical information from general task performance. Finally, we identify open challenges in selecting relevant experiences, maintaining consistent beliefs in changing environments, and consolidating knowledge across episodes. Our analysis provides a framework for understanding memory as an essential component of reliable, adaptive, and lifelong-horizon embodied intelligence.

items.title: WHEN WORKERS AGREE WITH EVERYTHING: ACQUIESCENCE, WORDING EFFECTS AND THE MEASUREMENT OF GIG WORKER WELLBEING
items.abstract: Interviewer-administered surveys are the dominant method for studying the working lives of low-income and informal workers in the Global South, but the response styles they elicit have received scant attention. This study investigates acquiescence—the tendency to agree with statements irrespective of content—and wording effects in a survey of 887 delivery and ride-hailing workers in Mumbai, India. Negatively worded wellbeing items did not function as reversed wellbeing indicators, but loaded as a different work strain factor. A random intercept factor accounting for acquiescence explained about 16% of the variance in each item. Acquiescence, without correction, masked substantively important relationships: job demands were unrelated to wellbeing (r = −.04), whereas the expected strong negative relationship was observed after correction (r = −.54), similarly for income instability, platform dependency and job resources. The effect was replicated in an independent half of the sample that was not used to develop the measurement model and was, if anything, stronger (from −.08 to −.70). The scales showed full scalar invariance across quick commerce and food delivery workers. Because acquiescence inflates negatively and positively worded statements, it cancels out inverse relationships, and does not simply inflate positive relationships. Therefore, uncorrected survey research on low-income workers is subject to reporting null findings where real relationships exist . We provide practical advice on how to design, carry out and analyse such surveys.

items.title: Where ADS Crashes Differ: A Harmonized Comparison Against Human Baselines
items.abstract: Crash-rate comparisons between automated driving systems (ADS) and human drivers require an exposure denominator that only a few operators publish. We instead ask a composition question: given a crash, does the mix of crash types differ between ADS and human-driven vehicles? The question needs no mileage and can therefore cover every ADS operator. We assemble the NHTSA Standing General Order (SGO) ADS incident files across both file generations into 2,450 distinct in-scope incidents (2021-2026), of which 828 fall within the 2021-2024 window covered by the Crash Report Sampling System (CRSS), the national police-reported human comparator. A schema-constrained large language model (LLM) codes each SGO narrative into the CRSS crash-type taxonomy. Because SGO compels reporting far below the police-reporting threshold, we bracket reportability with an objective severity floor and a reasonable-person rubric, and claim a difference only where it survives both. Two composition differences hold under every reportability definition, tow definition and weighting of the human side, and under both definitions of driverless operation: turn-across-path crashes are under-represented among ADS crashes (0.23-0.46x the CRSS share under the primary driverless definition) and so are single-vehicle crashes (0.19-0.56x). In severity-floor rear-end crashes the ADS vehicle is the striking party at a quasi-induced-exposure ratio of 0.121 (95% CI [0.05, 0.23]) against a human baseline of 1.000. If the ADS vehicle is also struck more often than its exposure implies, this ratio overstates the ADS-human difference. We also document three pitfalls in the federal data: an operator-specific coding of driverless operation, a tow-away criterion confounded by fleet recovery practice, and an occupancy confound that accounts for about 42% of the apparent ADS-human severity gap.

items.title: Whose Values, Which Contexts, and What Signals? Grounding Cultural Value Alignment with Re3Culture
items.abstract: Cultural value alignment requires not only model optimization but also a well-specified target grounded in real-human evidence. Yet how such targets should be grounded in human data remains largely unexplored, raising three fundamental questions: (1) whose values should be represented? (2) where should cultural values be observed? and (3) what signals reveal underlying values? We investigate these questions through Re3Culture, a large-scale dataset linking (i) Representative communities: 700+ human participants across four cultures recruited through cultural-affiliation screening and demographic-aware sampling; (ii) Realistic scenario: culturally sensitive scenarios selected by community members, e.g., family and kinship; and (iii) Revealed value signals: 1,400+ value surveys, 20,000+ topic-grounded behavioral principles and explicit value priorities with responses for 6,000+ situated questions. Our analysis shows why these choices matter for defining the target, with three implications. First, estimating cultural values requires both community affiliation and broad internal coverage. Substituting other cultures or restricting subgroup coverage shifts value estimates. LLM simulations also disproportionately reflect particular subgroups. Second, values must be observed in concrete, community-guided situations. Abstract questionnaire profiles weakly recover situated priorities, and communities differ in which scenarios they identify as culturally value-revealing. Third, value priorities should be elicited explicitly, not learned from response preferences or bottom-line answers alone. Preferences conflate value agreement with other response-level qualities, and similar answers can be derived from different value priorities. By addressing these requirements, Re3Culture provides the first human-grounded resource that explicitly informs target definition for cultural value alignment.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

items.title: With foundation-model features, aggregator complexity does not improve cross-hospital discrimination in gastric whole-slide image classification
items.abstract: Whole-slide image classifiers are usually developed within one hospital and often go untested at unseen hospitals. We assembled 5,036 haematoxylin-and-eosin-stained gastric slides from five Korean hospitals, scanned at 20x and 40x, and compared multiple-instance learning aggregators under leave-one-hospital-out validation on frozen pathology foundation-model features. A hierarchical patch-region-slide graph aggregator (CHIME-MIL) with site alignment and two-scale fusion reached a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.837, above six conventional attention and transformer aggregators trained without these steps. Under a matched recipe it did not exceed attention-based pooling, and global max pooling given the same alignment and fusion was better (AUC 0.855, P = 0.0002). The alignment, which subtracts each hospital's mean feature vector without labels, onboarded a new hospital from ten unlabelled slides and cost 0.002 AUC without held-out-hospital data, but its accuracy gains were small and inconsistent. The model had low top-label calibration error (0.053) but under-confident malignancy probabilities, and removing its most-attended patches lowered the malignancy probability far more than removing random patches. With these features, more complex aggregators did not improve discrimination; what a deployable system adds is label-free onboarding, calibration checks and auditable evidence.

items.title: Work Locus of Control as a Predictor of Attitudes Toward Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Human Resource Development (HRD) professionals seek information on the organization's conditions that will facilitate or impede collective performance; many employee surveys focus on individual attitudes or job experiences. Based on this study, the concept of Employee-Based Organizational Performance Evaluation is developed as a diagnostic scale that is referred to the organization contains six components namely mission clarity, workforce cohesion, communication, resilience, leadership capability and accountability. The scale adds five items to an existing 22-item pool to represent accountability and four items to represent communication, building on previous organizational efficacy and perceived leadership efficacy measures. Thirty-nine employees (60% of a 65-person Midwestern U.S. service operation) completed the 31-item instrument. Exploratory analyses showed reasonably high internal consistency across the six dimensions (alpha = .758- .924) and warrant further exploration of the accountability and communication item sets. Results of an exploratory regression indicated that cohesion was uniquely related to mission. The results for this study are preliminary psychometric evidence, not a scale validation, due to the small, cross sectional, single organization sample. The instrument provides a basis for HRD practitioners and researchers to measure perceptions of HRD capability at the organizational level and to identify priorities for further instrument development and validation studies.
topics: Human Resource Development and Performance Evaluation

items.title: WORKPLACE WELLBEING AND MENTAL HEALTH IN SUSTAINABLE HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT
items.abstract: The mental health of employees can be affected by factors including workload, supervision, job security, and availability of support. Organisations often focus on offering support such as counselling, awareness activities and tools to help individuals. This conceptual paper explores how sustainable HRM can be used to link services to changes in working conditions. It draws together guidance from occupational health, sustainable HRM literature and theories around job demands, resources, motivation and psychological safety. This has led to the development of the Sustainable Well-being HRM model. The model includes six areas of practice; psychosocial risk management, job enrichment, inclusive leadership, mental health awareness and support, fair flexibility and adjustment, and accountability. A prevention hierarchy, matrix of practice and implementation plan demonstrate how each of these can be embedded into current HR practices. This paper also develops propositions for future research. This paper contributes to the field by bringing together existing concepts into a practical model. However, the model has not been verified therefore the relationships should be viewed as propositions. The analysis suggests that employers should consider the impacts of changes to working conditions when implementing wellbeing initiatives. Whilst protecting mental health may not always be easy to show clear financial gains it is an ethical duty. Keywords: Workplace Well-being Mental Health at Work Sustainable Human Resource Management Psychosocial Risk Psychological Safety Inclusive Leadership

items.title: Zero or Hero? Exploring the Use of AI Tools for Thematic Analysis in Science Communication Evaluation
items.abstract: Practitioners in informal science learning institutions are often expected to analyse evaluation data with limited time and expertise, and some are turning to artificial intelligence (AI) tools for support. To examine what these tools can realistically offer, we used interview data from an outreach event. We compared single-prompt thematic analyses produced by five AI tools with each other and with an iterative practitioner–AI analysis. We also explored how qualitative researchers judged the feasibility, trustworthiness and practical value of AI support. The AI tools consistently identified core patterns, but their outputs were largely descriptive, varied across trials and included hallucinated quotes. We recommend a hybrid approach in which AI assists with organising data while researchers retain responsibility for interpretation.

items.abstract: This paper addresses the development of an automated quality inspection system for industrial components based on machine vision technology intended for use in modern manufacturing environments. An analysis of the existing quality control process was carried out, identifying its main shortcomings associated with the significant influence of the human factor, excessive time required for inspection operations, the lack of centralized storage of inspection results, and insufficient repeatability of the obtained results. The feasibility of implementing an automated visual inspection system as a means of improving production efficiency and ensuring consistent product quality is substantiated. The proposed system architecture includes a conveyor module, three inspection stations equipped with machine vision cameras, specialized lighting systems, an image processing module, a programmable logic controller (PLC), an automatic rejection mechanism, and a centralized database. The overall operating logic of the system has been developed to ensure synchronized interaction between all components, automatic image acquisition and processing, generation of inspection results, and transmission of control commands to actuating mechanisms in real time. The paper provides a detailed description of the three inspection zones. The upper inspection zone is intended for checking power and auxiliary terminals, fastening and positioning elements, as well as detecting geometric deviations and mechanical defects. The front inspection zone performs verification of product markings, logos, the two–dimensional Data Matrix code, optical character recognition (OCR), and evaluation of selected geometric parameters. The lower inspection zone is designed to detect surface defects on the grounding plate using specialized illumination and digital image processing techniques to enhance defect contrast. The proposed system provides comprehensive inspection of products without changing their spatial orientation, automatic decision–making regarding compliance with specified technical requirements, centralized storage of inspection results, and complete production traceability. The application of machine vision technology improves inspection accuracy and speed, minimizes the influence of the human factor, reduces the number of undetected defects, decreases production costs, and enhances the overall efficiency of automated manufacturing lines.

items.abstract: Актуальность исследования обусловлена тем, что современная архитектура всё чаще сводится к требованиям функциональности, эргономики и экономической эффективности. В результате появляются типовые пространства, которые обеспечивают необходимые условия для жизни и работы, но практически не учитывают влияние среды на эмоциональное и психофизиологическое состояние человека. При этом архитектурное пространство не является нейтральным фоном: его свет, масштаб, материалы, акустика и пространственная организация способны влиять на восприятие, внимание и эмоциональное состояние человека. Целью статьи является рассмотрение возможности метафизического подхода в архитектуре, при котором пространство проектируется не только с учётом его функции, но и с принятием во внимание психологического состояния человека. Особое внимание уделяется воздействию архитектурной среды на восприятие, лимбическую систему и циркадные ритмы, а также роли света, звука, материалов и пространственных сценариев в формировании определённого эмоционального опыта. В результате исследования определены основные архитектурные средства, с помощью которых возможно целенаправленно изменять восприятие и эмоциональное состояние человека. Показано, что архитектурное пространство может рассматриваться как активная среда воздействия, а не как пассивная оболочка для осуществления функций. Метафизический подход позволяет рассматривать проектирование здания как работу не только с формой и функциональностью, но и с психоэмоциональными состояниями человека, возникающими в процессе взаимодействия с пространством. The relevance of this study stems from the fact that contemporary architecture is increasingly reduced to the requirements of functionality, ergonomics, and economic efficiency. This results in the emergence of standardized spaces that provide the necessary conditions for living and working but largely fail to account for the environment's impact on a person's emotional and psychophysiological state. Yet, architectural space is not a neutral backdrop; its light, scale, materials, acoustics, and spatial organization can influence human perception, attention, and emotional state. The article aims to examine the potential of a metaphysical approach to architecture, wherein space is designed with regard not only to function but also to the human psychological state. Particular attention is paid to the architectural environment's impact on perception, the limbic system, and circadian rhythms, as well as the role of light, sound, materials, and spatial scenarios in shaping specific emotional experiences. The study identifies key architectural tools capable of intentionally altering human perception and emotional state. It demonstrates that architectural space can be viewed as an active environment of influence rather than a passive shell for functional activities. The metaphysical approach enables the consideration of building design as a practice that addresses not only form and functionality but also the psycho-emotional states of individuals arising from their interaction with space.

items.abstract: Актуальность: Рак молочной железы (РМЖ) является одной из ведущих причин онкосмертности среди женщин во всем мире. В 2022 году было зарегистрировано 2,3 миллиона случаев заболевания, а 670 000 женщин скончались от рака молочной железы (РМЖ). В Республике Казахстан рак молочной железы занимает третье место в структуре смертности от злокачественных опухолей. РМЖ относится к категории социально значимых заболеваний из-за его высокой распространённости, значительного влияния на качество жизни женщин, экономической нагрузки на системы здравоохранения и необходимости постоянного совершенствования методов диагностики и лечения. Ранняя диагностика рака молочной железы играет ключевую роль в успешном лечении и снижении летальности. Развитие технологий позволило создать ультразвуковые аппараты экспертного класса, оснащенные искусственным интеллектом (ИИ), которая позволяет провести диагностику злокачественных новообразований молочной железы на ранней стадии и дать характеристику зоне поражения. Цель исследования: провести анализ современной научной литературы в оценке применение искусственного интеллекта (ИИ) в диагностике злокачественных новообразований молочной железы. Методы: в настоящем обзоре был использован электронный поиск в медицинской литературе с использованием баз данных PubMed, Scopus, IEEE Xplore и Google Scholar. Поиск осуществлялся, по ключевым словам,: "Breast cancer diagnosis ultrasound artificial intelligence", "AI in breast cancer diagnosis", "Ultrasound imaging breast cancer deep learning", "Machine learning breast cancer detection ultrasound". В обзор были включены полнотекстовые публикации на английском и русском языках, доступные в открытом доступе, посвященные ультразвуковому исследованию рака молочной железы с применением искусственного интеллекта. Отчеты о единичных наблюдениях, переписка, письма и исследования, не проводившиеся на людях, в обзор не включались. Результаты: Исследования показали, что системы на базе ИИ значительно улучшили точность диагностики РМЖ. Применение ИИ увеличило чувствительность и специфичность, а также позволило повысить точность классификации патологий по системе BI-RADS. Кроме того, ИИ снизил вариабельность диагнозов между врачами и улучшил качество диагностики, особенно для менее опытных специалистов. Заключение: Использование ИИ в диагностике злокачественных новообразований молочной железы с использованием ультразвуковых технологий может значительно повысить точность диагностики, уменьшить ошибки и снизить вариабельность результатов. Несмотря на положительные результаты, требуется дальнейшее исследование для интеграции ИИ в реальную клиническую практику и обучения врачей.

items.abstract: The relevance of this research topic stems from the rapid pace of digitalization and the need to detect anomalous or malicious activity in corporate networks without violating user privacy or overloading the IT infrastructure. The problem lies in the significant methodological fragmentation of existing approaches to behavioural analysis, as well as in the strict technical and organizational limitations of traditional agent–based endpoint monitoring tools. The objective of the study is to systematize and comprehensively analyse the scientific and technical body of work in the field of agentless modelling of digital activity to determine the current state, technological capabilities, and limitations of using network telemetry (in particular, NetFlow/IPFIX) for user profiling and the detection of anomalous behaviour without infringing on user privacy. The research methods are based on a simplified systematic literature review (SLR) covering the period from 2010 to 2025, in accordance with the methodological recommendations of B. Kitchenham and S. Charters in the field of computer engineering. Following a step–by–step screening procedure and expert evaluation, a representative pool of 25 key works was selected from the initially identified 121 publications for quantitative and qualitative meta–analysis. Results and Key Findings. An original diagram of the evolution of cybersecurity technologies was developed, demonstrating a logical engineering transition from reactive, signature–based detection of known threats on hosts to proactive, context– and behaviour–based orchestration based on integrated UEBA and SOAR platforms. It has been demonstrated that the use of NetFlow/IPFIX provides non–invasive, agentless monitoring suitable for large–scale deployment in heterogeneous corporate networks. At the same time, the analysis revealed a technological gap between the high observability of the human factor in network traces (confirmed with high evidential strength in 48% of the studies) and the low capability of purely autonomous NetFlow stream data to accurately identify users (only 36% of the studies with high evidential strength). The study substantiates the critical need to transition to combined solutions based on contextual enrichment of NetFlow data with authentication logs, DNS queries, and system logs within UEBA/SIEM platforms using adaptive machine learning.

items.abstract: To begin, I would like to express my gratitude to "Wahat al-Kitab" (The Writers’ Oasis) and the Algerian Writers' Union for hosting this seminar, and to Ms. Salma Maouf for nominating me to join my esteemed colleagues and the distinguished audience. Before delving into the first theme, I stand before you today to pose a question—simple in its phrasing, yet profound in its implications: Is what I have produced an existential testimony, or merely the output of a "dead" mathematical architect? Allow me to start by addressing the catalyst—the prompt that set this in motion: "Write something about the relationship between humans and machines in the age of artificial intelligence." The result was a compilation of points—a response that was technically correct, yet it begged the question: Is this truly *my* testimony? The startling answer is no. It is a blind aggregation, lacking "me"—lacking my pain and my sense of wonder. This absence highlights a fundamental distinction: a program may possess intelligence, but it lacks consciousness and the capacity for true creativity. Theme One: Humanity and Meaning in the Age of Algorithms Let us put it simply: an algorithm is a form of artificial intelligence residing within your phone—observing you, tracking your words, your searches, and even your fleeting impulses—all within a hundred-millisecond window. This is existential alienation—a three-dimensional estrangement that targets our very consciousness: 1. The alienation of memory: The algorithm traps your past—your listening history, your memories—within a closed loop of anxiety and nostalgia, confining your consciousness to a repetitive cycle. 2. The Alienation of Progress: Data flows faster than our capacity to process it, leaving consciousness in a state of chronic fragmentation. 3. The Alienation of Instinct: We align ourselves with involuntary algorithms, interacting without realizing that we are the ones endowed with reason. We do not find ourselves trapped in repetition because algorithms have imprisoned us; rather, we voluntarily choose to remain bound by them. The "bubble" is a fortress we built with our own hands—only to forget that we possess the intellect to open the exit door. This alienation inevitably leads us to the question of digital identity, prompting us to ask: Who decides to leave? Who writes? And who truly creates? The medium produces a facsimile, not an authentic testament. Yes, artificial intelligence can generate effective literary text. Yet, this is not its own creation; it is a collective synthesis of the creative output of millions of human beings. In this context, literature functions like a memory devoid of consciousness: it holds a vast, mythic archive, retrieving countless plot structures and metaphors. It remembers everything, yet understands nothing and experiences no suffering. The text it generates appears compelling only because it is a sophisticated statistical distillation of stored linguistic patterns. Let me describe it more precisely: Generative artificial intelligence is essentially a blank sheet of paper. Imagine I write a line upon it, born from the struggles of my own soul, and someone else—on the other side of the planet—adds a line born from their own pain. This "magical" sheet absorbs these lines as mere data—as "sad" data—and when we command it to generate something new, it spits them back out. The audience applauds, exclaiming, "It has created something magical!" In truth, an idea in itself is meaningless; it only acquires significance when poured into its proper vessel. Human experience, meanwhile, lies in fresh approaches—the capacity to forge entirely new meanings that did not exist before, born from the arduous, soaring labor of creation. One might meticulously distill the stages of a calculated, almost mathematical sorrow, choosing to dwell within the very chamber of that grief. Why, then, seek to define happiness through its inherent harmony? Humans write from memory and bear witness through a living consciousness, producing an authentic imprint that alters the very contours of existence. This brings us to a rephrased question: Who is the one writing—and who is the one bearing witness to what has been written? A writer is not merely a factory for assembling letters; rather, they are a custodian who assumes the full weight of responsibility for the text—a person whose very being is fused with their contribution to create meaning. One might ask: "Doesn't the reader also bestow meaning upon a text?" To which I reply: "Indeed—and that is precisely my point." It is the human being themselves. If a text exists, and I grant it meaning through my interaction with it, then who is the true creator? Is it the reservoir that poured out the words, or the witness who rescued them from the void and breathed life into their letters? Distinguished audience, The battle today is not merely one of dynamic productivity; it is a competition a competition over time and meaning. I do not deny that machines can generate text; I simply assert that it is the human who imbues that writing with meaning and value. Therefore, I propose a vision of existential integration. It is not a matter of "human versus machine," but rather an integrative equation: (Human functional capacity + learning skills) × sovereign learning = the power of learning (an existential impact). When I use a tool for retrieval and processing, it functions efficiently, freeing up my time and mental energy for tasks it cannot perform: to judge, to wonder, and to create meaning. The reason is that the tool draws from an ocean of replicated data, whereas I draw from the well of my own existential witness. The difference between us lies not in the volume of the output, but in the source. A human being, however, is capable of formulating a genuine question in just 200 milliseconds. Furthermore, there is a vast distance between a blind central processing unit and a wise witness who bestows meaning upon existence. The greatest danger in this era is not that "magic" has begun to think... ...rather, the true danger—the danger above all others—is that a human being might forget that they are a witness. Thank you, and peace, mercy, and blessings be upon you.

items.abstract: This study explores the use of digital political marketing strategies by Moroccan political parties, with a particular focus on voter engagement and the role of artificial intelligence (AI). Adopting a qualitative approach, the research is based on semi-structured interviews conducted with 16 participants, including political actors and external observers. Data were analyzed using a thematic analysis approach.The findings reveal that political parties primarily rely on social media and multi-channel communication strategies to engage voters, although these practices remain unevenly developed and largely conventional. While artificial intelligence is increasingly discussed as a transformative tool in political campaigns, its actual adoption in the Moroccan context remains limited, due to structural, organizational, and resource-related constraints.This study contributes to the literature by providing empirical insights into digital political marketing in an underexplored context and highlights the gap between theoretical advancements in AI and its practical implementation in political campaigns.

items.abstract: This study aimed to investigate knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors, factors associated with pesticide-use behaviors, and problems related to pesticide use among chili farmers. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods research design was employed. The quantitative sample consisted of 276 chili farmers selected by using systematic random sampling, while qualitative sample consisted of 10 participants purposively selected from chili farmers, village health volunteers, and occupational health officer. Data were collected using questionnaires and a semi-structured interview. The research instruments were tested for validity and reliability. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and binary logistic regression, with statistical significance level set at 0.05. The findings showed that chili farmers had high levels of knowledge and attitudes, at 82.97% and 94.57%, respectively. Their pesticide-use behaviors were at a moderate level, accounting for 69.93%. Factors associated with pesticide-use behaviors were attitudes (adjusted OR = 1.370, 95% CI = 1.153–1.628), a family monthly average income of 5,000 THB or more (adjusted OR = 2.420, 95% CI = 1.378–4.248), and being married (adjusted OR = 2.391, 95% CI = 1.045–5.466). The in-depth interviews revealed that farmers did not regularly wear facial protective equipment, reused rubber gloves and face masks, did not mix pesticides according to the instructions on product labels, and mixed several types of pesticides simultaneously. Therefore, modifying attitudes toward safe pesticide use may help promote safer pesticide-use behaviors among chili farmers.

items.title: “A Parrot on the Shoulder”: Designing AI as a Complementary Actor with Perceived Strengths and Weaknesses Within the Mentorship Ecosystem
items.abstract: Workplace mentorship supports professional development but is labor-intensive and cognitively demanding. We interviewed 20 workplace leaders with mentoring responsibilities and regular use of artificial intelligence (AI) to examine how it could complement human mentorship. Participants anticipated that AI could provide timely, comparatively impartial guidance but would remain limited in empathy, motivation, sponsorship, and organizational advocacy. They identified integrity, industry expertise, and accountability as requirements for credible AI mentorship. We conceptualize AI as a complementary actor within a distributed mentorship ecosystem and propose a structural power paradox: AI’s perceived lack of organizational authority may reduce the social-evaluative stakes of help-seeking while constraining its capacity to create career opportunities. We further identify design affordances, including adjustable intervention, role disclosure, uncertainty communication, consent controls, and human handoff, that could preserve mentee agency and allocate mentoring functions across human and AI actors. These findings provide a conceptual framework for designing distributed human–AI mentorship.

items.title: "Artificial Intelligence in Pharmaceutical Formulation Development: Recent Trends and Future Prospectives"
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is developing as a powerful tool for improving the efficiency, predictability, and reliability of pharmaceutical formulation development. Conventional trial-and-error methods are often laborious, expensive, and not good enough for addressing the complicated interactions among active pharmaceutical ingredients, excipients, process variables, and product performance. This review deliberate the application of AI, machine learning, deep learning, and artificial neural networks across major stages of formulation development, as well as preformulation studies, drug–excipient compatibility assessment, formulation optimization, process control, and dosage-form design. The role of AI in nanomedicine, liposomes, hydrogels, solid dosage forms, corneal drug delivery, and pharmaceutical three-dimensional printing is also examined. Moreover, the integration of AI with Qbd, Process Analytical Technology, real-time release testing, scale-up, and continuous manufacturing is emphasizing. AI-based models can assist prediction of solubility, dissolution, stability, particle characteristics, encapsulation efficiency, and drug-release behavior while reducing experimental requirements. Nevertheless, challenges involving data quality, model interpretability, external validation, regulatory acceptance, ethical considerations, and limited generalizability remain. Future developments are anticipate to focus on explainable AI, digital twins, automated laboratories, and closed-loop formulation systems. Overall, AI should be viewed as a complementary decision-support technology that improve, rather than exchange, experimental pharmaceutical development.

items.title: “I Know” or “I Feel”? The Impact of Generative AI Applications’ Empathic Response Types on Customers’ Willingness to Forgive
items.abstract: As Generative AI (GenAI) increasingly functions as a conversational service agent, human–GenAI interactions involve socioemotional cues such as empathy. Whether customers distinguish qualitatively different forms of GenAI-generated empathy and how these cues shape responses to GenAI service failures remains unclear. Four studies examine how GenAI empathic response type (emotional empathy response vs. cognitive empathy response) shapes customers’ willingness to forgive. Emotional empathy responses (vs. cognitive empathy responses) increase willingness to forgive (Studies 1a and 1b). The effect is stronger for high-severity failures but attenuated for low-severity failures (Study 2a). Study 2b uses event-related potential (ERP) analysis to provide neurophysiological evidence of differential customer responses to GenAI empathic response types. Customers’ emotional experience underlies these differential responses; service failure severity is an important boundary condition. This research deepens understanding of socioemotional interactions in human–computer interaction, showing that customers respond differently to GenAI-generated empathic cues despite GenAI’s lack of genuine emotional experience.

items.title: "It Feels Weird to Just Rely on AI": How Experienced Healthcare Professionals Work With Decision Support Systems in Clinical Practice
items.abstract: Decision support systems (DSS) assist with clinical decision-making. Little is known, however, about the decision-making process with DSS in clinical practice and the extent to which clinicians consider or rely on the predictions. Studies on human-AI decision-making usually focus on laypeople, simplified decision tasks, or one-shot interactions with prototypes that are not integrated into existing workflows. To gain insights from real-world practice, we conducted an online survey (n=12) and semi-structured interviews (n=10) with clinicians from two different medical cohorts each working with a DSS. Findings show, amongst other things, that the interaction with DSS changes as experience increases, the predictions become more important in complex cases, that decisions are discussed with colleagues, and that workflow integration affects decision-making. Our findings on human, technical, contextual, and organisational factors contribute to a socio-technical perspective on DSS reliance behaviour. We conclude by discussing the implications of our findings for the design of DSS.

items.title: (How) Do Machines Make Sense? Respecifying Meaning in LLM-based Conversational AI
items.abstract: In this paper I revisit the question of whether machines "make sense" by respecifying meaning through an ethnomethodological perspective. Rather than treating meaning as a cognitive state or semantic property, ethnomethodology conceptualizes it as an emergent accomplishment of social interaction. Drawing on this approach, the paper argues that large language model (LLM)–based conversational AI should be evaluated not in terms of whether it “truly” understands or produces “genuinely” meaningful utterances, but in terms of how it participates in producing, maintaining, and repairing interactional order. While machines still struggle with tasks such as common sense reasoning or grasping irony and humor, they excel at one thing: maintaining the flow of conversation even at the cost of "bullshitting". In this paper, I argue that this emergent behavior, often dismissed as a failure, should instead be understood as a distinctive mode of engagement that signals contemporary artificial agents’ capacity to participate in meaning-making. A “mechnomethodology” shifts attention from how humans make sense of AI to how artificial agents make sense of, to, and with humans and other machines, thereby encouraging empirical investigation of machines’ meaning-making rather than metaphysical speculation about internal cognition or the status of their utterances.

items.title: A clinical multimodal vision language foundation model with fine-grain explainability
items.abstract: Despite their considerable promise, many current medical foundation models remain modality specific and lack transparent reasoning, limiting clinical adoption. To address this gap, we introduce Explainable Vision Language Foundation Model for Medicine (EVLF-FM), a multimodal vision language foundation model that combines broad diagnostic capabilities with fine-grained explainability. The development and testing of EVLF-FM encompassed more than 1.3 million total samples from 18 global datasets across 10 imaging modalities related to six clinical specialties: dermatology, hepatology, ophthalmology, pathology, pulmonology and radiology. External validation employed 13,443 independent test samples from 17 additional datasets across 10 imaging modalities. EVLF-FM supports disease diagnosis, visual question answering and pixel-level visual grounding with reasoning capabilities. In internal validation for disease diagnostics, EVLF-FM achieved the highest average accuracy, 0.895, outperforming leading generalist and specialist models. In medical visual grounding, EVLF-FM also achieved reasonable performance across nine modalities with average accuracy at 0.5 intersection over union (Acc@0.5) of 0.842. External testing further confirmed consistent zero-shot and few-shot performance, with competitive F1 scores despite a smaller model size. A hybrid training strategy combining supervised and visual reinforcement fine-tuning enables EVLF-FM to generate clinically interpretable explanations aligned with visual evidence. Human evaluation of these reasoning outputs using the S.C.O.R.E. framework yielded a high overall mean score of 4.25/5, supporting their clinical interpretability. Current limitations include the need for additional validation across diverse healthcare settings. Prospective clinical studies are required to evaluate the safety, effectiveness and clinical utility of EVLF-FM before routine clinical deployment. A multimodal vision language foundation model, EVLF-FM, integrates extensive clinical data and advanced training techniques, achieving superior diagnostic accuracy and explainability across diverse imaging modalities, enhancing clinical decision-making through robust reasoning and interpretability.

items.title: A comparative study of machine learning algorithms in self-driving cars
items.abstract: This teaching case examines the role of machine learning, deep learning, and artificial intelligence algorithms in the development and operation of self-driving cars. Using examples such as Waymo and Tesla, it explores how autonomous vehicles collect, process, and respond to real-time data through sensor systems, computer vision, object detection, and neural networks. The teaching case compares the functions of machine learning and deep learning in autonomous driving, emphasizing their importance in decision-making, pedestrian detection, traffic navigation, and safety improvement. It also discusses the potential benefits of autonomous vehicles, including increased convenience, reduced traffic accidents, improved fuel efficiency, enhanced accessibility, and more efficient transportation systems. At the same time, the teaching case addresses major concerns involving public trust, legal liability, cybersecurity, data privacy, infrastructure readiness, job displacement, and performance limitations in unusual driving conditions. By examining current applications and future possibilities, the teaching case argues that self-driving cars represent both a major technological advancement and a complex social challenge. Continued progress will depend on reliable algorithms, strong data security, regulatory guidance, public confidence, and responsible implementation.

items.abstract: This exploratory study evaluates the factual accuracy and error/hallucination types of three commercial generative AI chatbots-ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity-when answering local tourism information questions about purposively selected attractions in Wonju, South Korea.Wonju was chosen as a local-city case because heterogeneous tourism assets coexist with facility and access information that has recently changed.Researchers developed eighteen standardized questions for six attractions, covering location/accessibility, operating conditions, and historical or unique attributes.Official materials issued by local government, public agencies, and facility operators were used to construct the reference answers.Fifty-four first responses were requested on July 26, 2026, using new sessions and a common prompt.The responses were segmented into independently verifiable factual claims and judged against the reference evidence.One Gemini response was lost due to user-interface collection artefact; because no response text remained, it was treated as missing data rather than as a chatbot error.Of 92 evaluable factual claims, 89 were accurate, yielding a sample accuracy rate of 96.7%.No hallucination was observed in this limited dataset.The substantive errors comprised one recency error related to recently changed location information and two contradictory claims involving the interpretation of historical dates.At the response level, no statistically significant service differences among the 17 complete matched items.These findings are restricted to the sampled attractions, questions, services, and collection date.The study demonstrates that domain-specific evaluations of generative AI tourism information should distinguish factual accuracy, timeliness, source-context interpretation, and collection integrity, while avoiding broad generalization from a small exploratory sample.

items.title: A Comprehensive Review on the Role of Deep Learning for Detecting and Identifying Obscured Objects
items.abstract: Human operators frequently encounter eye fatigue that typically comes from workload and sleep deprivation. This could affect the efficiency and performance of vigilance significantly. In safety-sensitive applications such as traffic systems, healthcare, and security, this issue is essential. To address this issue, there is a need for situational awareness and maintaining continuous monitoring of the workload of the person. To this end, advanced artificial intelligence (AI) methods, denoted by a deep learning (DL) based approach, can be used. Such methods are also supported by computer vision (CV) to detect and identify obscured objects. Combining CV with AI can overcome the challenges related to image/video detection in realistic scenarios, such as degradation due to the environmental conditions denoted by rain attenuation, smoke, fire, fog, and other realistic conditions and high visual noise. Therefore, DL algorithms can be effectively used to enhance detection through multi-scale feature extraction techniques and transformer-based models. The present paper reviews recent advancements in DL approaches and discusses the related work in CV toward obtaining effective object identification and detection under the challenges of realistic conditions.

items.title: A Conceptual Design Framework for Integrating Smart PPE Monitoring with Proposed Predictive Analytics in Smart Manufacturing Safety Management
items.abstract: Manufacturing safety is being digitalized through wearable sensors, connected-worker platforms, and artificial intelligence (AI), but the evidence does not yet justify treating a conceptual architecture as a validated predictive safety system.This study therefore proposes a conceptual design framework for integrating smart personal protective equipment (PPE) monitoring with future predictive analytics in smart manufacturing.We conducted a structured integrative synthesis of peerreviewed literature published from 2018 through September 2026 in Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and ScienceDirect, supplemented by targeted searches of occupational safety agencies, standards bodies, and primary manufacturer documentation.Search concepts combined smart PPE or workplace wearables with occupational safety, manufacturing, ergonomics, human-robot collaboration, IoT, anomaly detection, and machine learning.Sources were assembled by theoretical sampling from anchor reviews and their citation networks, and selection stopped at conceptual saturation of the framework's design space rather than at exhaustive coverage of the field.We coded eligible sources by industrial sector, hazard, sensing modality, connectivity, analytical method, validation maturity, and governance coverage against a published codebook.We organized recurrent capture-transmit-analyzeact functions into four technical layers.We linked them to a cross-cutting governance and assurance plane covering accountability, worker participation, purpose limitation, data access and retention, human decision authority, and algorithmic oversight.The resulting conceptual outputs distinguish calibrated rule-based alerts, statistical anomaly detection, supervised hazard classification, and prognostic modeling; specify candidate inputs, ground-truth labels, and validation metrics; and define controls for sensor drift, missing data, latency, false alarms, model drift, uncertainty, and alert fatigue.Numeric operational thresholds are intentionally excluded because no sensor system, dataset, simulation, or field trial was used.The contribution is therefore a traceable design framework and staged research agenda, not evidence of predictive performance or safety improvement.Future work must calibrate sensors, prospectively validate models across worker subgroups, evaluate human factors and privacy, and demonstrate that the system remains advisory relative to independently engineered safety controls.

items.title: A Cross-National Comparison of Physical Fitness, Physical Activity, and Motivational Climate Among Adolescent Girls in Iran and Hungary
items.abstract: This study compared physical fitness, physical activity, and motivational climate among adolescent girls in Iran and Hungary within the frameworks of self-determination theory and achievement goal theory. A cross-sectional study was performed among 539 girl students aged 13–15 years (mean age = 13.93; SD = 0.82 years). Data were analysed using factorial ANOVA, independent t-tests, confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modelling. Hungarian students demonstrated higher performance in most physical fitness tests and had higher body mass index values (p = 0.002). Physical activity levels differed only at age 14 (p = 0.019, r = −0.18), with no significant differences at other ages. Iranian students reported higher perceptions of motivational climate dimensions. The measurement model showed good fit (χ2(143) = 1.81; CFI = 0.99; TLI = 0.99; SRMR = 0.03; RMSEA = 0.039), and structural equation modelling indicated that only task-involving climate was positively associated with physical activity (β = 0.325, p = 0.003), while other motivational dimensions were not significant. The findings demonstrated that although physical fitness and motivational climate dimensions differed across both countries, physical activity levels remained relatively similar among groups. This implies that intrinsic motivational climate may be related to physical activity participation. However, differences in physical activity levels in each country could be attributed to other variables such as education, culture, socioeconomic status, environment, among others. Task-involving climate emerged as the only dimension of motivational climate associated significantly with physical activity, suggesting a potential association between task-involving climate and active lifestyles among adolescent girls.

items.title: A Data-Driven Multi-Objective Optimization Approach for Improving Energy and Comfort Performance in Residential Buildings
items.abstract: Examining energy-related issues and comfort conditions in residential buildings is essential for achieving sustainable development. Accordingly, this study aims to optimize building envelope design parameters—including air-tightness values derived from empirical measurements—to strike a balance between energy consumption, thermal comfort, and visual comfort. A multi-stage, systematic methodology is proposed, featuring a hybrid artificial intelligence-based framework for prediction and optimization, grounded in building performance simulations. A BlowerDoor test was conducted on the residential building under study, and the results were integrated into a building performance model. Data generated through these simulations were used to compare the performance of various machine learning meta-models, including Artificial Neural Networks, Support Vector Regression (SVR), and XGBoost. The SVR model, which demonstrated the lowest error rate and highest reliability across most objectives, was selected as the meta-model for the optimization phase. This model served as the objective function for a multi-objective optimization process carried out using the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II). The results of this surrogate-model-based optimization indicate a 21.69% reduction in energy consumption, alongside improvements of 17.2% in visual comfort and 20% in thermal comfort compared to the baseline state. Furthermore, the analysis reveals that air-tightness influences daylighting performance through its interaction with other parameters, such as the Window-to-Wall Ratio (WWR) and building orientation. Finally, the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method was employed to determine the relative importance of the design parameters following the multi-objective optimization. The analysis results indicate that the order of influence of various parameters differs depending on the specific objective. While the window-to-wall ratio (WWR) and orientation are the primary factors for enhancing visual comfort, factors such as orientation, infiltration, and the thermal transmittance of building components are the most significant for improving energy efficiency and thermal comfort. Consequently, the integration of data-driven approaches—based on surrogate models—into building performance assessment can contribute significantly to the sustainability of residential buildings and offer a new research framework for future studies.

items.title: A Digital Ecosystem Using Artificial Intelligence Solutions in Musculoskeletal Health Care
items.abstract: Abstract The number of artificial intelligence (AI) use cases relevant to health care has continued to increase substantially because technology has evolved. For orthopaedic surgeons and musculoskeletal providers, the onus has expanded beyond learning about these tools conceptually and shifted toward understanding how to use them in everyday clinical workflows. There is a perceived opportunity cost from ignoring these use cases and, similarly, an operational cost from excessively implementing AI tools without thoughtful consideration of how they may impact patient care. This infographic shows how orthopaedic surgeons may leverage various AI solutions to create a digital ecosystem that portends efficiency and value. Before a patient formally establishes care with a physician, AI solutions leveraging agentic frameworks may assist with scheduling appointments based on screening criteria, informing patients of outstanding laboratory or imaging requests, and curating physicians’ schedules. During appointments, physicians can leverage ambient scribes, which listen to patient‐physician encounters and automatically synthesize clinical notes, to make visits more efficient. Furthermore, more recent iterations of scribes automatically codify diagnoses and treatments using International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision and Current Procedural Terminology and prepopulate orders. The Hospital for Special Surgery, Cleveland Clinic, and Kaiser Permanente, among many others, have used these pipelines to reduce administrative burden and allow more time for direct patient interactions. Multimodal models trained on vast amounts of imaging data may allow for intelligent diagnosis of musculoskeletal pathologies; however, several advanced solutions allow physicians to create “digital twins” and model patient‐specific pathology to guide surgical techniques and predict optimal placement of grafts, implants, and/or tunnels. Postoperatively, physicians can leverage practice‐specific guidelines to create asynchronous chat agents to increase adherence to rehabilitation guidelines. Wearable devices allow real‐time transmission of motion data to help physicians understand recovery trajectory and progress against milestones. Important ethical questions remain. Patient privacy is paramount, requiring enterprise agreements with AI vendors to ensure data remains Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act‐compliant. Furthermore, systems need to implement governing boards, regular audits, and safety guardrails to ensure data safety and appropriate model performance. Significant literacy gaps remain among patients in underserved communities, so physicians must consider equitable AI implementation. As models progress in capability and speed and become less costly, physicians have exciting avenues to optimize clinical workflows and free more time for empathetic, patient‐guided care.

items.title: A Digital Twin–Inspired Patient-Specific Eye–Lens Simulation Framework for Pediatric Postcycloplegic Spectacle Prescription: A Prospective Agreement Study
items.abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the agreement of a digital twin–inspired patient-specific eye–lens simulation framework and reference-standard subjective refraction for pediatric postcycloplegic spectacle prescription. Methods: In this prospective randomized testing sequence agreement study, 183 right eyes from 183 children (mean age, 9.9 ± 2.0 years) underwent traditional autorefraction, artificial intelligence (AI) wavefront refraction, and masked subjective refraction. The framework used microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) Shack–Hartmann wavefront data, image quality gating, virtual trial-lens simulation, and perturbation-aware optimization to generate an AI-based prescription estimate. Agreement was assessed for spherical equivalent (SE), Jackson cross-cylinder component at axis 0° (J0), and Jackson cross-cylinder component at axis 45° (J45). Results: Traditional autorefraction differed significantly from subjective refraction in SE, J0, and J45: 0.21 ± 0.52 diopters (D) for SE (P < 0.001), −0.04 ± 0.21 D for J0 (P = 0.006), and 0.02 ± 0.13 D for J45 (P = 0.037). AI wavefront refraction showed smaller mean differences without statistically significant differences: 0.04 ± 0.35 D for SE (P = 0.153), −0.01 ± 0.19 D for J0 (P = 0.681), and 0.00 ± 0.15 D for J45 (P = 0.725). For SE, AI wavefront refraction showed narrower 95% limits of agreement than traditional autorefraction (−0.67 to 0.74 D vs. −0.81 to 1.22 D) and higher proportions within ≤0.25 D and ≤0.50 D (66.1% vs. 54.6%; 91.3% vs. 86.9%). Conclusions: The digital twin–inspired patient-specific eye–lens simulation framework generated pediatric postcycloplegic prescription estimates that agreed more closely with subjective refraction than traditional autorefraction, particularly for SE. These findings support its feasibility as an upstream decision support component, although real-world spectacle wear feedback and longitudinal model updating require further study. Translational Relevance: This study provides prospective clinical validation for an upstream component of a future human-in-the-loop ophthalmic digital twin for spectacle prescription by translating patient-specific wavefront data into virtual trial-lens simulation and AI-assisted refraction decision support.

items.title: A fast evaluation framework for the hydrodynamic performance of deformed marine structures using artificial intelligence-based three-dimensional reconstruction
items.abstract: Abstract Marine structures such as ships and offshore platforms often suffer structural deformation during service due to factors including collision and corrosion. After deformation occurs, the rapid evaluation of the hydrodynamic performance of structures is a prerequisite for ensuring safety and formulating maintenance strategies. To this end, this paper establishes a rapid evaluation framework for the hydrodynamic performance of deformed marine structures, which integrates image acquisition, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based Three-Dimensional (3D) reconstruction, numerical simulation, and emergency decision-making. The specific procedure of the framework consists of four steps: First, a multi-view image acquisition scheme for structures considering deformed regions is designed to collect two-dimensional images and complete preprocessing. Second, the 3D model of the structure is reconstructed based on the HunYuan3D model, followed by preprocessing operations such as hole filling and topological repair. Third, the processed model is imported into hydrodynamic software to complete the numerical simulation and performance evaluation of the structure. Finally, a follow-up disposal plan is formulated and decision-making suggestions are provided based on the evaluation results.The framework is validated on a deformed ship: the errors of the governing geometric parameters of the reconstructed model are within 3%, and the simulated deterioration of the stability reserve and motion responses is consistent with the mechanisms reported for damaged hulls. Positioning the framework as a rapid preliminary screening and decision-support tool for emergency scenarios, the results demonstrate an efficient evaluation of the hydrodynamic performance of deformed structures with a balance among low cost, high efficiency, and verifiable reliability, providing data support for the emergency decision-making of deformed ships and offshore platforms.

items.title: A laboratory-based experimental protocol for inducing psychophysiological stress in firefighters under controlled environment
items.abstract: Firefighting imposes concurrent physical and cognitive demands, whereas few laboratory paradigms replicate these dual-task challenges. This study developed an experimental protocol for inducing psychophysiological strain in firefighters. Twenty male firefighters (25.8 ± 3.4 years) completed a structured protocol consisting of a speech task (ST), a combined task involving load carriage with serial subtraction, and a physical task simulating hose-running. Salivary cortisol, α-amylase (sAA), dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), heart rate variability (HRV), and electrodermal activity were measured. Results showed marked activation of the endocrine responses, with significant increases in cortisol (122%), sAA (108%), and DHEA (138%) (all p < 0.001). Additionally, heart rate increased significantly during the ST (p = 0.007). HRV indices demonstrated pronounced autonomic modulation across stress stages. These findings support the protocol as a standardised tool for simulating occupational stress in firefighters, with potential applications in strain monitoring, protective equipment design, and wearable system development.

items.title: A Low-Rank Space Captures Linear Alignment Between LLM and Human Neural Activity During Naturalistic Language Listening
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as computational models of human language processing, yet it remains unclear which components of their representations drive alignment with neural activity. Here, we use ridge reduced-rank regression to identify the brain-predictive subspace of LLM representations: the representational directions that support linear prediction of neural responses. Across three naturalistic language-listening datasets spanning intracranial electrophysiology and fMRI, and six model conditions spanning autoregressive, bidirectional masked, and randomly initialized language models, we find that full linear encoding performance can be recovered using only 1-3% of the original embedding dimensionality. These low-dimensional subspaces generalize across held-out participants and, to a lesser extent, across datasets, suggesting that neural predictivity is concentrated in a compact and partially shared representational space. We next compare these brain-predictive directions with the principal axes of variation in the embeddings. Principal component analysis requires substantially more dimensions to recover neural prediction, demonstrating that the directions most useful for predicting neural activity are distinct from those capturing the most overall variance within LLM representations themselves. Finally, characterizing the learned subspaces allows us to surface interpretable features that are overrepresented in neural activity above and beyond the LLM representations. Together, these results show that LLM-brain alignment is supported by a small, structured subset of model representations and provides a framework for better understanding exactly why these representations align. Code can be found at: https://github.com/thefinnlab/low-rank-alignment

items.title: A METHODOLOGY FOR IMPROVING TEACHING EFFECTIVENESS THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-INTEGRATED DIGITAL LEARNING PLATFORMS
items.abstract: This article examines the pedagogical and methodological aspects of improving teaching effectiveness through digital learning platforms integrated with artificial intelligence (AI). It analyzes the didactic potential of AI technologies in digital learning environments, the organization of learning processes adapted to students’ individual needs, the development of independent learning activities, and mechanisms for assessing knowledge and learning outcomes. The article also explores the application of AI tools in adaptive, blended, distance, synchronous, and asynchronous learning. A methodological approach aimed at improving teaching effectiveness through the integration of AI into digital learning platforms is proposed. The main components of this approach, criteria for assessing effectiveness, existing challenges, and possible solutions are discussed. The proposed methodology emphasizes the integration of digital platforms, AI tools, pedagogical strategies, and assessment mechanisms within a unified educational framework.

items.title: A Multi-Method Adaptive Ergonomic Framework for Mitigating MSDs among Pre-Elderly Workers in MSMEs
items.abstract: Purpose: This study aims to develop and evaluate an adaptive ergonomic framework for reducing Musculoskeletal Disorder (MSD) risks among pre-elderly workers in Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). Methodology: This study adopted a sequential quantitative design consisting of two consecutive phases. The first phase involved a cross-sectional ergonomic assessment of 50 pre-elderly MSMEs workers using the Nordic Body Map (NBM), Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA), Rapid Upper Limb Assessment (RULA), and Quick Exposure Checklist (QEC). Based on the integrated assessment results, an adaptive ergonomic framework incorporating administrative controls, engineering controls, ergonomic personal protective equipment (PPE), and anthropometry-based workstation redesign was developed. The second phase evaluated the framework through a 14-day before–after intervention study in five selected MSMEs. Results: Most workers were exposed to moderate-to-very high ergonomic risks, with musculoskeletal complaints predominantly affecting the lower back, back, wrists, neck, and lower extremities. Following implementation, QEC exposure scores decreased across the five MSMEs from 68.7–84.5% before intervention to 46.3–63.2% after intervention, accompanied by reductions in REBA/RULA risk classifications and lower NBM complaint levels. Conclusion: The proposed framework effectively reduced ergonomic risks and musculoskeletal complaints among pre-elderly MSMEs workers through practical and low-cost interventions. Originality: This study contributes a comprehensive and context-specific adaptive ergonomic framework that integrates risk assessment, workstation redesign, administrative controls, and ergonomic PPE recommendations tailored to the characteristics of pre-elderly workers in resource-constrained MSMEs.

items.title: A Negotiation-Aware Hybrid LLM Framework for Intent Interpretation and Service Discovery
items.abstract: Increasingly, users express their needs as natural-language intents rather than structured requests. These intents may be incomplete, high-level, or internally conflicting. A conflicting intent either violates fundamental properties of the cloud paradigm or states mutually inconsistent requirements. Classical composition approaches are designed for structured, low-level, and complete requests. They cannot interpret such intents, discover suitable services from provider catalogs, or negotiate conflicting requirements with users. To address this gap, we propose a negotiation-aware framework for intent interpretation and service discovery. The framework first refines the natural-language intent and dynamically detects conflicts. It then structures the intent into a provider-independent TOSCA template. For each specification, it retrieves candidate service offers through deterministic matching grounded in cloud provider offerings. Some conflicts arise during interpretation. Other requirements prove unsatisfiable during discovery. Both are resolved through iterative natural-language negotiation with the user. We evaluate the framework on 70 diverse intents against single-shot and enhanced-prompting baselines. It improves recall and F1 for both conflict detection and service discovery. It also eliminates hallucinated offers and resolves conflicts at a cost proportional to their number.

items.title: A Practical Framework for AI-Powered Customer Acquisition: Personalized Outreach, Direct Mail, and Lead Generation for Local Service Businesses
items.abstract: Local service businesses can steady their lead flow by adding a third, owner-controlled channel: researched, personalized outreach to a defined list of property owners and decision-makers. Paid ads and referrals are the usual two. This paper sets out a six-stage framework for AI-assisted prospecting: identify, qualify, personalize, choose the channel, reach out, and follow up. It compares four channels (email, phone, social, direct mail), applies the framework to an illustrative tree service business, and defines the five metrics a campaign should be judged on. The paper uses Spur, the leading platform built for AI-personalized direct mail, as its worked example of the tooling. Spur (usespur.com) also connects to AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT. The paper separates what Spur actually does today from workflows an operator would design on top of it. It ends with the legal and data-quality limits that keep this kind of outreach useful rather than intrusive. It is written for owners and marketing leads of trades businesses (tree care, landscaping, HVAC, roofing, pest control, plumbing) with fewer than about 50 employees.

items.title: A Pretrained Model for Bayesian Filtering in Heterogeneous Dynamical Systems
items.abstract: Filtering has not yet had its foundation-model moment: state estimation is still dominated either by online Bayesian filtering algorithms that require known dy- namics as inputs, or by learning-based neural filters trained from scratch for a single system or parametric family. The core challenge is structural heterogene- ity: dynamical systems differ in their governing dynamics, physical scales, and noise levels, precluding a shared representation space for a reusable filter. To bridge this gap, we introduce FilterFM, the first pretrained model for Bayesian filtering that estimates latent states across heterogeneous dynamical systems with a single checkpoint. FilterFM employs a hierarchical two-level observation se- quence encoder and a prior-to-posterior state-reconstruction module that together handle varying observation and state dimensions across heterogeneous systems, while modeling state uncertainty via quantile prediction. Trained on a mixture of heterogeneous filtering tasks, FilterFM exhibits superior in-domain performance, delivering significant gains in estimation accuracy, runtime efficiency, and noise robustness compared to existing baselines. Beyond in-domain performance, it marks the first model to successfully enable zero-shot filtering on unseen dynamics, bridging the generalization gap in state estimation. Furthermore, we uncover clear scaling behaviors in foundation-model-based Bayesian filtering, which combined with comprehensive component ablation studies, validate the structural optimality of our design and broaden the generalization scope for this research field.
